name: DBIX
tagline: 1990s multi-user ANSI SQL server from Halcyon Software for Windows and a long list of Unix variants.
description: DBIX was a commercial client/server SQL database sold by Halcyon Software in the mid-1990s as a low-cost alternative to the big RDBMS vendors. It ran on Windows 3.x, NT and 95 as well as SunOS, Solaris (SPARC and x86), AIX, HP-UX, Digital UNIX, SCO and Linux, and offered transaction logging, crash recovery, record-level locking, ANSI SQL and an ODBC interface, with extra cursor-sharing extensions on Windows. It was positioned as the back end for Halcyon's VBIX tools, which ported Visual Basic-style applications to Unix. The product disappeared around the end of the decade and the vbix.com domain is now parked, so it is of historical interest only.
statusNote: Sold by Halcyon Software c. 1996-1999; no releases or vendor site since, and vbix.com is now a parked domain.

pricing.notes: Was sold as a packaged commercial server; no longer available.

strengths: Unusually broad 1990s platform list: Windows plus most commercial Unixes and early Linux
Transaction log, crash recovery and record-level locking at a budget price point
Standard ODBC interface rather than a proprietary API
weaknesses: Discontinued for over two decades; no binaries, documentation or support remain
Never built a third-party tool or community ecosystem
useCases: Historical reference on low-cost 1990s SQL servers
Identifying legacy systems that still reference DBIX data files
